$comment: Table of contents for the documentation published at https://proxybrowser.ubaidbinwaris.com/docs. Each page is docs/site/<slug>.md; scripts/sync-docs.mjs copies them into the website at build time.

pages.title: Introduction
pages.description: What Proxy QA Browser is: a free, open-source desktop QA browser for testing your own forms from verified US locations, on real devices and browsers.

pages.title: Install
pages.description: Download and run Proxy QA Browser on Windows 10 and 11, Linux (AppImage) and macOS 12 or later, with first-launch steps, moving to another computer and uninstalling.

pages.title: First run
pages.description: The first-run set-up wizard: bundled browsers, optional proxy keys stored in the encrypted vault, the Manage keys window and a tour of the main window.

pages.title: Launching browsers
pages.description: Launch an isolated browser through a verified exit IP: the Launch page, live sessions, run results with network capture, history and saved profiles.

pages.title: Proxy providers
pages.description: Use DataImpulse, Bright Data, Oxylabs, Decodo or IPRoyal: products and logins, username syntax, sticky and rotating sessions, and custom gateways.

pages.title: Locations and devices
pages.description: Target a US state, city or ZIP code, verify the exit IP against it before the window opens, and emulate any of 226 phone, tablet and desktop presets.

pages.title: Browsers
pages.description: Bundled Chromium, Firefox and WebKit plus installed Chrome, Edge, Brave, Opera and Vivaldi: one-click installs, detection, custom paths and known limits.

pages.title: Site access tokens
pages.description: Send a secret header only to the origins you list, so your own WAF, CAPTCHA or fraud scoring can recognize and allow your QA traffic.

pages.title: Updates
pages.description: How signed online and USB updates are verified with Ed25519 and SHA-256, the computer copy, the startup update check and updating on macOS.

pages.title: Scenarios and matrices
pages.description: Record QA scenarios, add variables and datasets, run browser × device × location matrices, compare screenshots, schedule runs and export reports.

pages.title: Compliance, accessibility and performance checks
pages.description: Automated consent and TCPA disclosure checks, consent checkbox and lead-certificate script checks, axe-core accessibility rules and performance budgets.

pages.title: Self-healing selectors
pages.description: How self-healing selectors work: recorded fallback locators, healed steps flagged in results, warn or fail modes, and updating a scenario in one click.

pages.title: CI runner
pages.description: Run exported scenarios and suites headless in CI with the command-line runner, the Docker image or the GitHub Action, with JSON, JUnit and HTML reports.

pages.title: MCP server
pages.description: Connect Claude Code, Cursor or another MCP client so an AI assistant can run geo- and device-aware QA checks, limited to the origins you allow.

pages.title: Security and privacy
pages.description: The AES-256-GCM credential vault and OS keychain, what is never logged, Electron hardening, every network connection the app makes and where data is stored.

pages.title: Settings reference
pages.description: Reference for every Proxy QA Browser setting: where it lives, its default and allowed range, QA automation policy limits and environment variables.

pages.title: Troubleshooting
pages.description: Fix common problems when installing and starting, with proxies and locations, browsers, sessions, the vault and QA automation, and look up error codes.

pages.title: FAQ
pages.description: Answers to common questions about Proxy QA Browser: cost, responsible use, data and privacy, proxy plans and providers, browsers, devices and security.

pages.title: Architecture
pages.description: How Proxy QA Browser is built: the Electron process model and IPC contracts, source layout, start-up, a launch step by step, providers, data and security.

pages.title: Contributing
pages.description: Set up a development environment, run the tests, follow the code conventions and project scope, add a proxy provider and open a pull request.

pages.title: Building and releasing
pages.description: Build the Windows EXE, Linux AppImage and macOS DMG, sign update manifests with Ed25519, publish tagged releases through CI and deploy the website.
